full_judgment: 12. The object of rule 30 of Order 41 CPC is to see that a judge does not act callously or even mechanically. Its purpose is to put the judge on the right track and to that extent rules of procedure can do it to see that he acts judicially. The 1st Appellate Court is supposed to consider the merits of the evidence independently with a clear consciousness of relevant points which arose for adjudication. It is also to afford the parties an opportunity of knowing and understanding the grounds of the decision to enable them to move the higher forum and to enable the High Court to judge whether lower Appellate Court has properly appreciated and decided the case. The 1st Appellate Court is expected to give its own decision specially on materials relating on facts which would be self explanatory and in the nature of speaking order. It is not enough to merely opine that there is nothing wrong with the finding of the Trial Court. However, affirming judgment need not enter into detailed reasons to the same extent as that of the judgment of reversal. In a judgment of affirmance it is not necessary to record exhaustively all the reasons advanced in the judgment of the Trial Court. The crucial test is to see whether the Appellate Court has applied its mind to all salient facts and points for decision.
